# AiBox.DevPortal

## Project Purpose

AiBox.DevPortal is a local AI-assisted development portal built with Blazor and Radzen.

Its primary goal is to provide a structured environment for planning, generating, reviewing, verifying, and applying software changes using local AI models running on AI-Box infrastructure.

The portal acts as an orchestration layer between developers, local LLMs, project knowledge, project history, and code-generation workflows.

---

## Core Architecture

AiBox.DevPortal follows a service-oriented, feature-driven architecture.

### Workflow

Planner
→ Task Plan
→ Task Slices
→ Patch Preview
→ Verification
→ Apply Changes
→ Project History

All new development should support and extend this workflow.

### Major Systems

#### Local Coder

Provides AI-assisted development capabilities including:

* Planning
* Task decomposition
* Patch generation
* Verification
* Execution history

#### Project Knowledge Index

Maintains searchable knowledge about the repository structure and codebase.

#### Project History Index

Stores completed features, pending work, implementation history, and recommended next slices.

#### Verification Pipeline

Validates generated changes before they are applied to the project.

---

## Technology Stack

### Backend

* .NET 9
* ASP.NET Core
* Blazor Server-Side Rendering (SSR)

### UI

* Radzen Blazor Components
* Responsive component-based layouts

### AI Integration

* Ollama
* Local LLMs
* Planner / Patch Builder / Reviewer / Verifier workflows

### Storage

* JSON-based project metadata
* Local file storage
* Project indexes

---

## Solution Structure

### Components

Blazor and Radzen user interface components.

Keep UI logic minimal and delegate business operations to services.

### Services

Contains business logic and orchestration.

Examples include:

* TaskDecompositionService
* TaskSliceExecutionService
* TaskSliceVerificationService
* ProjectKnowledgeIndexService
* ProjectHistoryIndexService
* PatchIntentService

### Models

Application models, DTOs, execution requests, execution results, and index structures.

Examples include:

* TaskPlan
* TaskPlanSlice
* TaskSliceExecutionRequest
* TaskSliceExecutionResult
* ProjectKnowledgeIndex
* ProjectHistoryIndex

### Data

Runtime storage, indexes, backups, and generated artifacts.

### Tests

Unit and integration tests validating business workflows.

---

## Development Rules

### General

* Prefer small, incremental slices.
* Build before considering work complete.
* Maintain nullable reference safety.
* Use dependency injection.
* Use async/await for I/O operations.
* Avoid business logic inside Razor components.

### UI

* Prefer Radzen components.
* Keep pages focused on presentation.
* Move reusable logic into services.

### Services

* Encapsulate business rules in services.
* Avoid duplicating logic.
* Reuse existing services before introducing new ones.

### Models

* Keep models simple and focused.
* Use explicit request/result types for workflows.

---

## Build and Validation

### Build

```bash
dotnet build
```

### Run

```bash
dotnet run
```

### Tests

```bash
dotnet test
```

### Completion Criteria

A feature is considered complete when:

* The solution builds successfully.
* No new warnings or errors are introduced.
* Relevant tests pass.
* The feature integrates with existing workflows.
* Project history and knowledge indexing impacts are considered.

# AiBox.DevPortal

## Project Purpose

AiBox.DevPortal is a local AI-assisted development portal built with Blazor and Radzen.

Its primary goal is to provide a structured environment for planning, generating, reviewing, verifying, and applying software changes using local AI models running on AI-Box infrastructure.

The portal acts as an orchestration layer between developers, local LLMs, project knowledge, project history, and code-generation workflows.

---

## Core Architecture

AiBox.DevPortal follows a service-oriented, feature-driven architecture.

### Workflow

Planner
→ Task Plan
→ Task Slices
→ Patch Preview
→ Verification
→ Apply Changes
→ Project History

All new development should support and extend this workflow.

### Major Systems

#### Local Coder

Provides AI-assisted development capabilities including:

* Planning
* Task decomposition
* Patch generation
* Verification
* Execution history

#### Project Knowledge Index

Maintains searchable knowledge about the repository structure and codebase.

#### Project History Index

Stores completed features, pending work, implementation history, and recommended next slices.

#### Verification Pipeline

Validates generated changes before they are applied to the project.

---

## Technology Stack

### Backend

* .NET 9
* ASP.NET Core
* Blazor Server-Side Rendering (SSR)

### UI

* Radzen Blazor Components
* Responsive component-based layouts

### AI Integration

* Ollama
* Local LLMs
* Planner / Patch Builder / Reviewer / Verifier workflows

### Storage

* JSON-based project metadata
* Local file storage
* Project indexes

---

## Solution Structure

### Components

Blazor and Radzen user interface components.

Keep UI logic minimal and delegate business operations to services.

### Services

Contains business logic and orchestration.

Examples include:

* TaskDecompositionService
* TaskSliceExecutionService
* TaskSliceVerificationService
* ProjectKnowledgeIndexService
* ProjectHistoryIndexService
* PatchIntentService

### Models

Application models, DTOs, execution requests, execution results, and index structures.

Examples include:

* TaskPlan
* TaskPlanSlice
* TaskSliceExecutionRequest
* TaskSliceExecutionResult
* ProjectKnowledgeIndex
* ProjectHistoryIndex

### Data

Runtime storage, indexes, backups, and generated artifacts.

### Tests

Unit and integration tests validating business workflows.

---

## Development Rules

### General

* Prefer small, incremental slices.
* Build before considering work complete.
* Maintain nullable reference safety.
* Use dependency injection.
* Use async/await for I/O operations.
* Avoid business logic inside Razor components.

### UI

* Prefer Radzen components.
* Keep pages focused on presentation.
* Move reusable logic into services.

### Services

* Encapsulate business rules in services.
* Avoid duplicating logic.
* Reuse existing services before introducing new ones.

### Models

* Keep models simple and focused.
* Use explicit request/result types for workflows.

---

## Build and Validation

### Build

```bash
dotnet build
```

### Run

```bash
dotnet run
```

### Tests

```bash
dotnet test
```

### Completion Criteria

A feature is considered complete when:

* The solution builds successfully.
* No new warnings or errors are introduced.
* Relevant tests pass.
* The feature integrates with existing workflows.

# AiBox.DevPortal

## Project Purpose

AiBox.DevPortal is a local AI-assisted development portal built with Blazor and Radzen.

Its primary goal is to provide a structured environment for planning, generating, reviewing, verifying, and applying software changes using local AI models running on AI-Box infrastructure.

The portal acts as an orchestration layer between developers, local LLMs, project knowledge, project history, and code-generation workflows.

---

## Core Architecture

AiBox.DevPortal follows a service-oriented, feature-driven architecture.

### Workflow

Planner
→ Task Plan
→ Task Slices
→ Patch Preview
→ Verification
→ Apply Changes
→ Project History

All new development should support and extend this workflow.

### Major Systems

#### Local Coder

Provides AI-assisted development capabilities including:

* Planning
* Task decomposition
* Patch generation
* Verification
* Execution history

#### Project Knowledge Index

Maintains searchable knowledge about the repository structure and codebase.

#### Project History Index

Stores completed features, pending work, implementation history, and recommended next slices.

#### Verification Pipeline

Validates generated changes before they are applied to the project.

---

## Technology Stack

### Backend

* .NET 9
* ASP.NET Core
* Blazor Server-Side Rendering (SSR)

### UI

* Radzen Blazor Components
* Responsive component-based layouts

### AI Integration

* Ollama
* Local LLMs
* Planner / Patch Builder / Reviewer / Verifier workflows

### Storage

* JSON-based project metadata
* Local file storage
* Project indexes

---

## Solution Structure

### Components

Blazor and Radzen user interface components.

Keep UI logic minimal and delegate business operations to services.

### Services

Contains business logic and orchestration.

Examples include:

* TaskDecompositionService
* TaskSliceExecutionService
* TaskSliceVerificationService
* ProjectKnowledgeIndexService
* ProjectHistoryIndexService
* PatchIntentService

### Models

Application models, DTOs, execution requests, execution results, and index structures.

Examples include:

* TaskPlan
* TaskPlanSlice
* TaskSliceExecutionRequest
* TaskSliceExecutionResult
* ProjectKnowledgeIndex
* ProjectHistoryIndex

### Data

Runtime storage, indexes, backups, and generated artifacts.

### Tests

Unit and integration tests validating business workflows.

---

## Development Rules

### General

* Prefer small, incremental slices.
* Build before considering work complete.
* Maintain nullable reference safety.
* Use dependency injection.
* Use async/await for I/O operations.
* Avoid business logic inside Razor components.

### UI

* Prefer Radzen components.
* Keep pages focused on presentation.
* Move reusable logic into services.

### Services

* Encapsulate business rules in services.
* Avoid duplicating logic.
* Reuse existing services before introducing new ones.

### Models

* Keep models simple and focused.
* Use explicit request/result types for workflows.

---

### Build

```bash
dotnet build
```

### Run

```bash
dotnet run
```

### Tests

```bash
dotnet test
```

A feature is considered complete when:

* The solution builds successfully.
* No new warnings or errors are introduced.
* Relevant tests pass.
* The feature integrates with existing workflows.

```text
namespace AiBox.DevPortal.Services;

public sealed class ScheduledRunDispatcher : BackgroundService
{
    private static readonly TimeSpan PollInterval = TimeSpan.FromSeconds(30);

    private readonly IServiceScopeFactory _scopeFactory;
    private readonly ILogger<ScheduledRunDispatcher> _logger;

    public ScheduledRunDispatcher(
        IServiceScopeFactory scopeFactory,
        ILogger<ScheduledRunDispatcher> logger)
    {
        _scopeFactory = scopeFactory;
        _logger = logger;
    }

    protected override async Task ExecuteAsync(CancellationToken stoppingToken)
    {
        using var timer = new PeriodicTimer(PollInterval);

        while (!stoppingToken.IsCancellationRequested)
        {
            await ProcessDueRunsAsync(stoppingToken);

            if (!await timer.WaitForNextTickAsync(stoppingToken))
            {
                break;
            }
        }
    }

    private async Task ProcessDueRunsAsync(CancellationToken cancellationToken)
    {
        using var scope = _scopeFactory.CreateScope();
        var scheduledRunService = scope.ServiceProvider.GetRequiredService<ScheduledAgentRunService>();

        var nowUtc = DateTimeOffset.UtcNow;
        var dueRuns = await scheduledRunService.GetDueRunsAsync(nowUtc, cancellationToken);

        foreach (var run in dueRuns)
        {
            if (run.IsRunning)
            {
                continue;
            }

            try
            {
                var started = await scheduledRunService.MarkStartedAsync(run.Id, nowUtc, cancellationToken);
                if (started is null)
                {
                    continue;
                }

                _logger.LogInformation("Scheduled run {RunId} started.", run.Id);

                var completed = await scheduledRunService.MarkCompletedAsync(
                    run.Id,
                    DateTimeOffset.UtcNow,
                    cancellationToken);
                if (completed is null)
                {
                    continue;
                }

                _logger.LogInformation("Scheduled run {RunId} completed.", run.Id);
            }
            catch (Exception exception)
            {
                _logger.LogError(exception, "Scheduled run {RunId} failed during dispatch.", run.Id);

                try
                {
                    await scheduledRunService.MarkFailedAsync(
                        run.Id,
                        exception.Message,
                        DateTimeOffset.UtcNow,
                        cancellationToken);
                }
                catch (Exception markFailureException)
                {
                    _logger.LogError(markFailureException, "Failed to record failure for scheduled run {RunId}.", run.Id);
```
                }
            }
        }
    }
}

```text
namespace AiBox.DevPortal.Services;

public sealed class ScheduledRunDispatcher : BackgroundService
{
    private static readonly TimeSpan PollInterval = TimeSpan.FromSeconds(30);

    private readonly IServiceScopeFactory _scopeFactory;
    private readonly ILogger<ScheduledRunDispatcher> _logger;

    public ScheduledRunDispatcher(
        IServiceScopeFactory scopeFactory,
        ILogger<ScheduledRunDispatcher> logger)
    {
        _scopeFactory = scopeFactory;
        _logger = logger;
    }

    protected override async Task ExecuteAsync(CancellationToken stoppingToken)
    {
        using var timer = new PeriodicTimer(PollInterval);

        while (!stoppingToken.IsCancellationRequested)
        {
            await ProcessDueRunsAsync(stoppingToken);

            if (!await timer.WaitForNextTickAsync(stoppingToken))
            {
                break;
            }
        }
    }

    private async Task ProcessDueRunsAsync(CancellationToken cancellationToken)
    {
        using var scope = _scopeFactory.CreateScope();
        var scheduledRunService = scope.ServiceProvider.GetRequiredService<ScheduledAgentRunService>();

        var nowUtc = DateTimeOffset.UtcNow;
        var dueRuns = await scheduledRunService.GetDueRunsAsync(nowUtc, cancellationToken);

        foreach (var run in dueRuns)
        {
            if (run.IsRunning)
            {
                continue;
            }

            try
            {
                var started = await scheduledRunService.MarkStartedAsync(run.Id, nowUtc, cancellationToken);
                if (started is null)
                {
                    continue;
                }

                _logger.LogInformation("Scheduled run {RunId} started.", run.Id);

                var completed = await scheduledRunService.MarkCompletedAsync(
                    run.Id,
                    DateTimeOffset.UtcNow,
                    cancellationToken);
                if (completed is null)
                {
                    continue;
                }

                _logger.LogInformation("Scheduled run {RunId} completed.", run.Id);
            }
            catch (Exception exception)
            {
                _logger.LogError(exception, "Scheduled run {RunId} failed during dispatch.", run.Id);

                try
                {
                    await scheduledRunService.MarkFailedAsync(
                        run.Id,
                        exception.Message,
                        DateTimeOffset.UtcNow,
                        cancellationToken);
                }
                catch (Exception markFailureException)
                {
                    _logger.LogError(markFailureException, "Failed to record failure for scheduled run {RunId}.", run.Id);
                }
            }
        }
```
    }
}

```text
namespace AiBox.DevPortal.Services;

public sealed class ScheduledRunDispatcher : BackgroundService
{
    private static readonly TimeSpan PollInterval = TimeSpan.FromSeconds(30);

    private readonly IServiceScopeFactory _scopeFactory;
    private readonly ILogger<ScheduledRunDispatcher> _logger;

    public ScheduledRunDispatcher(
        IServiceScopeFactory scopeFactory,
        ILogger<ScheduledRunDispatcher> logger)
    {
        _scopeFactory = scopeFactory;
        _logger = logger;
    }

    protected override async Task ExecuteAsync(CancellationToken stoppingToken)
    {
        using var timer = new PeriodicTimer(PollInterval);

        while (!stoppingToken.IsCancellationRequested)
        {
            await ProcessDueRunsAsync(stoppingToken);

            if (!await timer.WaitForNextTickAsync(stoppingToken))
            {
                break;
            }
        }
    }

    private async Task ProcessDueRunsAsync(CancellationToken cancellationToken)
    {
        using var scope = _scopeFactory.CreateScope();
        var scheduledRunService = scope.ServiceProvider.GetRequiredService<ScheduledAgentRunService>();

        var nowUtc = DateTimeOffset.UtcNow;
        var dueRuns = await scheduledRunService.GetDueRunsAsync(nowUtc, cancellationToken);

        foreach (var run in dueRuns)
        {
            if (run.IsRunning)
            {
                continue;
            }

            try
            {
                var started = await scheduledRunService.MarkStartedAsync(run.Id, nowUtc, cancellationToken);
                if (started is null)
                {
                    continue;
                }

                _logger.LogInformation("Scheduled run {RunId} started.", run.Id);

                var completed = await scheduledRunService.MarkCompletedAsync(
                    run.Id,
                    DateTimeOffset.UtcNow,
                    cancellationToken);
                if (completed is null)
                {
                    continue;
                }

                _logger.LogInformation("Scheduled run {RunId} completed.", run.Id);
            }
            catch (Exception exception)
            {
                _logger.LogError(exception, "Scheduled run {RunId} failed during dispatch.", run.Id);

                try
                {
                    await scheduledRunService.MarkFailedAsync(
                        run.Id,
                        exception.Message,
                        DateTimeOffset.UtcNow,
                        cancellationToken);
                }
                catch (Exception markFailureException)
                {
                    _logger.LogError(markFailureException, "Failed to record failure for scheduled run {RunId}.", run.Id);
```
```text
                }
            }
        }
    }
}
```

# AiBox.DevPortal

## Project Purpose

AiBox.DevPortal is a local AI-assisted development portal built with Blazor and Radzen.

Its primary goal is to provide a structured environment for planning, generating, reviewing, verifying, and applying software changes using local AI models running on AI-Box infrastructure.

The portal acts as an orchestration layer between developers, local LLMs, project knowledge, project history, and code-generation workflows.

---

## Core Architecture

AiBox.DevPortal follows a service-oriented, feature-driven architecture.

### Workflow

Planner
→ Task Plan
→ Task Slices
→ Patch Preview
→ Verification
→ Apply Changes
→ Project History

All new development should support and extend this workflow.

### Major Systems

#### Local Coder

Provides AI-assisted development capabilities including:

* Planning
* Task decomposition
* Patch generation
* Verification
* Execution history

#### Project Knowledge Index

Maintains searchable knowledge about the repository structure and codebase.

#### Project History Index

Stores completed features, pending work, implementation history, and recommended next slices.

#### Verification Pipeline

Validates generated changes before they are applied to the project.

---

## Technology Stack

### Backend

* .NET 9
* ASP.NET Core
* Blazor Server-Side Rendering (SSR)

### UI

* Radzen Blazor Components

### AI Integration

* Ollama
* Local LLMs
* Planner / Patch Builder / Reviewer / Verifier workflows

### Storage

* JSON-based project metadata
* Local file storage
* Project indexes

---

* ProjectHistoryIndex

### Data

Runtime storage, indexes, backups, and generated artifacts.

Unit and integration tests validating business workflows.

* Prefer small, incremental slices.

```text
namespace AiBox.DevPortal.Services;

public sealed class ScheduledRunDispatcher(
    IServiceScopeFactory scopeFactory,
    ILogger<ScheduledRunDispatcher> logger) : BackgroundService
{
    private static readonly TimeSpan PollInterval = TimeSpan.FromSeconds(30);

    protected override async Task ExecuteAsync(CancellationToken stoppingToken)
```
```csharp
    {
```

```text
using AiBox.DevPortal.Models;

namespace AiBox.DevPortal.Services;

public sealed class SelectedContextValidator
{
    private static readonly HashSet<string> EditableExtensions = new(StringComparer.OrdinalIgnoreCase)
    {
        ".cs", ".razor", ".json", ".yml", ".yaml", ".css", ".html", ".js", ".md", ".csproj", ".sln", ".props", ".targets"
    };

    public void ValidateForPatchPreview(IEnumerable<LocalCoderFileContext> fileContexts)
    {
        var contexts = (fileContexts ?? [])
            .Where(file => file is not null)
            .ToArray();

        var editableFiles = contexts
            .Where(IsEditableSourceFile)
            .ToArray();

        if (editableFiles.Length == 0)
        {
            throw CreateValidationException("No editable source files selected.");
        }

        if (editableFiles.Any(file => file.IsTruncated))
        {
            throw CreateValidationException("Selected file context is incomplete. Patch preview requires full file contents.");
        }
    }

    private static bool IsEditableSourceFile(LocalCoderFileContext file)
    {
        if (file is null || string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(file.RelativePath))
        {
            return false;
        }

        if (file.IsGeneratedFile)
        {
            return false;
        }

        if (IsAgentInstructionsFile(file.RelativePath))
        {
            return false;
        }

        return EditableExtensions.Contains(Path.GetExtension(file.RelativePath));
    }

    private static bool IsAgentInstructionsFile(string relativePath)
    {
        return Path.GetFileName(relativePath).Equals("AGENTS.md", StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase);
    }

    private static PatchPreviewValidationException CreateValidationException(string message)
    {
        return new PatchPreviewValidationException(
            message,
            [message],
            string.Empty,
            string.Empty,
            string.Empty);
    }
}
```

The `CoderKnowledgePanel` currently lacks search filtering functionality. To implement this, we need to add logic that filters the list of indexed files based on user input for search text and kind.

### Files Likely Involved
- `CoderKnowledgePanel.razor`

### Step-by-Step Implementation Plan

1. **Add Search Filtering Logic**:
   - Add a method to filter the list of indexed files based on search text and kind.
   - Update the UI components to display filtered results.

2. **Update Razor Component**:
   - Bind the search text and selected kind to parameters.
   - Implement a computed property or method to generate the filtered list of items.

3. **Handle User Input**:
   - Bind the search text and kind inputs to the component's state.
   - Update the filtered list whenever the user changes the search text or kind.

4. **Update UI**:
   - Display the filtered list in the data grid.
   - Show a message if no items match the current filters.

### Safe Commands to Verify

1. **Build and Run the Project**:
   ```sh
   dotnet build
   dotnet run
   ```

2. **Navigate to the CoderKnowledgePanel**:
   - Ensure the panel is displayed correctly with the project knowledge index.
   - Test the search functionality by entering different search text and selecting different kinds.

```csharp
@code {
    // ... existing code ...

            && (selectedKind == "All" || item.Kind == selectedKind))
        .ToList() ?? new List<ProjectKnowledgeItem>();

    // ... existing code ...
}
```

```razor
<AppDataGrid Data="@FilteredItems" TItem="ProjectKnowledgeItem" PageSize="10"

    <Columns>
        <RadzenDataGridColumn TItem="ProjectKnowledgeItem" Property="RelativePath" Title="Relative Path" />

            <Template Context="item">@item.LastModifiedUtc.ToLocalTime().ToString("yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss")</Template>
        </RadzenDataGridColumn>
    </Columns>
</AppDataGrid>
```

```razor
<RadzenTextBox @bind-Value="searchText"

               Style="width: 100%;" />

<RadzenDropDown TValue="string"
                @bind-Value="selectedKind"
                Data="@KindOptions"
                Style="width: 100%;" />
```

The implementation plan involves adding search filtering logic to the `CoderKnowledgePanel` component. This will allow users to filter the list of indexed files based on search text and kind, enhancing the usability of the panel. The UI components will be updated to display the filtered results, and user input bindings will ensure that the filtering is applied dynamically.

# Local Coder History Component

The `LocalCoderHistory` component is used to browse and inspect saved Local Coder sessions. This component does not execute any Local Coder actions but provides a view of all recorded tasks with filters for status and search.

## Inputs
- **searchText**: A string used to filter records by title, repository, model, or instructions.
- **selectedStatus**: A `LocalCoderTaskStatus?` used to filter records by their status.

## Outputs
- **grid**: An instance of `AppDataGrid` that displays the list of records.

## Methods
- **LoadAsync()**: Asynchronously loads all Local Coder history records from the service.
- **OpenLocalCoder()**: Navigates to the main Local Coder page.
- **OpenLocalCoder(LocalCoderTaskHistoryRecord record)**: Navigates to a specific Local Coder session based on the provided record.
- **ExportMarkdown(LocalCoderTaskHistoryRecord record)**: Exports the selected record as Markdown and copies it to the clipboard.

```razor
<PageTitle>Local Coder History</PageTitle>
```
